narr: Training thunderstorms brought several rounds of torrential rainfall to portions of northeast Illinois on the 12th, especially around the interior Chicago metro area. Street flooding was reported around a number of municipalities. Nearly 500 service requests were made to the city of Chicago for water in basements. One person was also injured at Montrose Beach as lightning struck nearby.
ev: Several inches of water were covering roadways in the vicinity of LaGrange Rd and 55th St in Countryside.

Numerous reports of street flooding came out of Chicago's northside neighborhoods. Multiple underpasses were flooded along DuSable Lakeshore Drive, including at Montrose and Foster Avenues. Standing water was reported near the Sheridan CTA station. A handful of basement flooding reports also came out of the area. A private weather station in Lincoln Square recorded 2.82 of rain between 1 PM and 4:30 PM central standard time, 1.9 of which fell in a 90-minute period ending around 3 PM. Another private weather station in West Ridge recorded 1.8 in the same 90-minute period.
Multiple reports of street flooding were received out of La Grange and Brookfield.
Several dozen reports of flooded basements came out of Chicago's Gage Park and Chicago Lawn community areas.

A few reports of flooded basements were received out of the Dunning and Montclare community areas of Chicago. A photo shared via social media also showed 12 to 18 inches of standing water surrounding homes in Elmwood Park.

Multiple reports of flooded roadways came out of Mokena and Frankfort. Three separate private weather stations in the area recorded between 3.71 and 3.89 inches of rain between roughly 12:30 PM and 3 PM CST, featuring a couple of periods with rainfall rates of 2 inches per hour.

Numerous reports of flooding were received from the vicinity of Tinley Park, Oak Forest, and Homewood. A viaduct along Dixie Hwy in Homewood was flooded and closed to traffic. Water had risen up to car bumpers near Harlem and 167th St in Tinley Park. A private weather station in Homewood recorded 3.1 inches of rain between approximately 12:30 PM and 4:30 PM CST. A trained spotter in Country Club Hills recorded 2.38 inches in a 90 minute period.

Numerous reports of flooded yards and roadways came out of Woodridge, Downers Grove, and Westmont. Three separate private weather stations in the area recorded between 2.76 and 3.12 inches of rain between roughly 2 PM and 5 PM CST, most of which fell in a one hour period between 3:45 and 4:45 PM.
